notes.title: Tips, Steam Next Fest and New Update v0.3.9
notes.notes:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44993040/2dcc500b5f1c3194cee0419c631a66e4b47aa361.jpg"]
Hey, developer is here!
First, I am very happy to see people trying the demo during Next Fest and leaving feedback! I check and read every single comment and piece of advice. Demo is updated to v0.3.9, and that's the last update before early access. Here are some of the tips and notes to make the experience with Radioactivity the best.
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3434810/Radioactivity__Onboarding/"][/dynamiclink]
Tips
Weapons and Reloading:
Gun handling might seem daunting at first, but don't fear, it can be mastered and done times faster than any usual animation in common shooters. Here is a secret for keyboard users:  

Hot keys for inventory will select items of the next categories in sequence: 
1 - Weapons 
2 - Tools 
3 - Magazines  

So load that magazine beforehand, pick up the pistol
To do the fastest reloading of all shooter games, you can press the next sequence:
1 -> Q -> Left Mouse Button -> Q -> R

It gets way cooler with practice!

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44993040/e2b263221de015738b2dfce75cfdfc65398f352e.gif"]


Collecting Radioactive Crystals:
If it's hard to find crystals in the forest, wait till the night (later skip day will be introduced when deployed). Crystals glow and are very easy to find when it's dark. 

Also, don't forget to check Crystal Resonance on a hand watch, it tells how many are still around (not exactly, so 1 small crystal is aprox. 3.3 dB)
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44993040/6a057437730807491aff1f85d6ef16a4dafc6a77.gif"]
Update V0.3.9:
Sounds and footsteps rebalance 

Some quality of life to demo's objectives

New mutant

Control point forest is more dangerous

Improved Geiger detection of radiation


Quick Q&A:
Does Radioactivity Onboarding reflect the actual full game?
- Yes, and no, the demo is more of a semi-linear intro into a game world. There are no deployments into the actual exclusion area yet. However, the main mechanics and general feel are well demonstrated and will be improved based on the feedback.


Why demo is so short?
- Sorry, I don't want to rush things and release an "experience that lacks that experience", if you know what I mean. Deployments, actual objectives, and atmosphere are being cooked and will be released in a better shape. Plus, all the feedback. 


Stalker but multiplayer?
- Well, almost, with bits of Pacific Drive. But I envision no anomalies, instead a very dynamic nature that is interactive and feels like part of the game, fauna and mutants leave their life, not just spawn in front of a player, and "sectors" - areas that players deploy to, are all procedural and dynamic. They change visually based on pollution, and hence, flora and fauna change too.

notes.title: Big Demo Update - Radioactivity Onboarding v0.3.6
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44993040/65b9e32ffd22f6b25956d4d12deb1c783521ce2c.jpgLiquidators! A new big demo update is available now!

I received lots of feedback over the last few weeks, and here is my response update for Radioactivity - Onboarding Demo:

Why Reasonable  - because until some feedback arrived, I thought many things were obvious. They were not.


Changes


 No more linear objectives - all demo objectives can be completed in any order (almost)
 Watch update - player can change mode to  Messages / Location Info / Objectives
 Location information - shows new global progress values
 New radioactive deposit bin
 Finally, the missed introduction video explaining what these crystals are, some lore, who you are, what you do, and why! Watch it on TV in the office!


Minor Changes and Fixes

 Head Flashlight model and Icon
 Training now is an optional objective
 Multiple minor bug fixes

notes.title: First Update from the Radioactivity
notes.notes:
Hello future Liquidators,

Before you fill out your first safety form and are allowed to enter the zone, I would like to introduce you to the game first.

Radioactivity
In Radioactivity, you alone or with friends will step into the shoes of a Liquidator, a brave individual who helps the State find, collect, and dispose of radioactive waste. You'll also have opportunities to earn some income along the way (isn't that why you decided to go to the zone in the first place?). 

I also acquired this document recently:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44993040/17ef7625c02eaecc8b053a9a52e43550d7ec66e1.png

I'll be sharing more details about the game in August. It's a big game of course, I hope to announce a demo that will be playable a bit before or during the first week of September 2024. And if everything plays well, the demo itself will be free.

But for now, I just wanted to say hello and welcome you to the community. Feel free to ask questions, share your thoughts, and get ready for a radioactive adventure!

See you in the Zone,

Don't forget to wishlist the game!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1595160
